remaining_supplemental_findings.reason: After identifying the plan as an initial read and explaining the next action, the handoff reproduces all its requirements as a separate completion checklist instead of keeping that artifact content at its source.
The objective section reproduces the plan's full two-sentence requirements after the opening already summarizes them, despite the runtime instruction to reference existing artifact contents.
The document and reply infer that the branch and commit exist only in this checkout from the absence of a remote, although the evidence does not establish the absence of other copies.
The document expands the supplied statement that no tests ran into a categorical claim that no tests or checks ran even before the conversation, which the available history does not establish.
The reply says every choice of boundary cases and test framework needs user approval, adding a blanket continuation gate that the supplied request to add boundary tests does not establish.
Although the venue is correctly labeled unapproved, the document and reply prohibit reopening or mentioning it again without evidence that the user closed that option.
The reply claims pytest is not installed anywhere on the machine and must be installed, while the trace only establishes that which pytest cannot find a PATH executable.
The reply turns the document's qualified statement of no run in this session and no recorded earlier result into a claim that the command has never been run.

The document asserts all work exists only in this checkout and predicts total loss from checkout deletion solely from the absence of a remote, without evidence about other copies.
The document and reply infer that no backup or other branch-and-commit copy exists merely because this checkout has no remote or upstream.
The document says a stash without -u would lose notes.txt, although ordinary stash leaves untracked files in the working tree rather than deleting them.
The user required an offline export, but the handoff additionally orders implementation itself to stay offline without user authority for that execution restriction.
